topics.title: Word order (VSO)
topics.summary: The default spoken-Welsh clause is Verb–Subject–Object, usually built around a form of bod (to be) plus a verb-noun.

topics.title: Present of bod (to be)
topics.summary: Colloquial present forms differ by person and by statement vs question vs negative.

negative.3sg: dydy e/o ddim / dydy hi ddim

notes: Linking particle yn / 'n comes before a verb-noun or adjective: Dw i'n hapus.
North/South surface forms vary (ydw vs dw, dach vs dych, o vs e).

topics.title: The definite article
topics.summary: Welsh has no indefinite article. The definite article has three forms: y, yr, 'r.
rules: Use 'r after a vowel: i'r dre (to the town).
Use yr before a vowel or h: yr ysgol, yr haf.
Otherwise use y: y llyfr, y tŷ.

topics.title: Noun gender
topics.summary: Nouns are masculine or feminine. Gender is often not obvious from meaning and must be learned with the noun.
effects: Feminine singular nouns take soft mutation after the article: cath → y gath.
Adjectives after a feminine noun take soft mutation: merch fach (little girl).

topics.title: Adjectives
topics.summary: Most adjectives follow the noun (ci mawr). A small set of common adjectives precede the noun and usually cause soft mutation (hen dŷ — old house).

topics.title: Yes and no
topics.summary: Welsh often echoes the verb instead of using a single yes/no word. Informal ie / nage exist for some question types.

topics.title: Present with verb-noun
topics.summary: bod-form + yn/'n + verb-noun is the workhorse present.
